Guidance.reason: Guidance came in well above expectations. NVIDIA guided fiscal Q2 revenue to $1.35 billion (±2%), above the Street's roughly $1.28 billion consensus.

Revenue.reason: Revenue beat expectations. Q1 FY17 revenue rose 13% year over year to $1.305 billion, above the ~$1.26 billion consensus.

Product.reason: A major new product cycle got underway. NVIDIA launched its new Pascal architecture (GeForce GTX 1080/1070, Tesla P100, DGX-1), entering full production.

Profits and profitability.reason: Profitability beat expectations. Non-GAAP EPS rose 39% year over year to $0.46, above the $0.32 consensus, with gross margin also up year over year.

Costs.reason: Costs grew more slowly than revenue and profit, a sign of operating discipline. Non-GAAP operating expenses rose just 4% year over year (GAAP up 6%), per the underlying press release.

Debt, leverage and capital raise.reason: No debt or leverage concerns; the company kept returning capital to shareholders. NVIDIA entered a new $500 million accelerated buyback, part of $3.5 billion already returned.

Management.reason: Management struck a confident tone on growth. CEO Jen-Hsun Huang highlighted growth across all four platforms and called the new Pascal architecture a "giant boost" to deep learning, gaming, and VR.
